“Saint Joseph was the first adorer, the first religious. Although he never adored our Lord under the Eucharistic species, he did possess and adore Jesus in human form.” (St. Peter Julian Eymard)

Saint Joseph lived with Jesus for thirty years in the home of Nazareth, making it the first Christian monastery and adoration chapel. While his days were filled with hard carpenter's labor, his evenings and nights were passed in uninterrupted, loving contemplation of the Incarnate God.

Saint Joseph teaches us that genuine contemplation does not demand withdrawing from duties; rather, it turns ordinary work and daily family life into a ceaseless offering of adoration before God.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 23
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Model of Workmen, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: At the workbench where he [St. Joseph] plied his trade together with Jesus, Joseph brought human work closer to the mystery of the Redemption.
scripture_or_quote.author: St. John Paul II

reflection:
The devil hates an honest and diligent worker. At the beginning of human history, the wicked serpent initiated his attack on the human family in the workplace — that is, the garden God gave Adam and Eve to tend and keep. Lucifer hates work. He particularly disdains the fact that because of love, God humbled himself and became a man, making himself capable of manual labor.

Jesus is God. Together with the Father and the Holy Spirit, he made the heavens and the earth. When he became flesh, Jesus sanctified human work and elevated it to a level of greatness that did not exist prior to his Incarnation. In his humanity, he learned how to work as a man by imitating the example of his earthly father, St. Joseph.

**Saint Joseph is the model workman.** If St. Joseph taught the God-Man how to work, he is more than capable of serving as our model as well. Hard work benefits the person, the family, and society.

> *He [St. Joseph] belongs to the working-class, and he bore the burdens of poverty for himself and the Holy Family, whose tender and vigilant head he was.*  
> — Pope Pius XI

**Saint Joseph will teach you how to be a diligent worker.** However, neither Jesus nor St. Joseph were workaholics. Saint Joseph made time for God, family, recreation, and rest. He modeled these balanced aspects of human life for Jesus and will teach them to you as well.

> *Come to me, all who labor and are burdened, and I will give you rest.*  
> — Mt 11:28

reading.title: Saint Joseph the Worker
reading.content:
On May 1, 1955, Pope Pius XII instituted the feast of St. Joseph the Worker. In the mid-20th century, atheistic communism attempted to hijack May Day as a secular communist worker's day to spread class hatred and eliminate God from society.

Pope Pius XII elevated St. Joseph as the true guardian and patron of laborers, declaring: “The humble workman of Nazareth not only personifies before God and the Church the dignity of the man who works with his hands, but is always the provident guardian of you and your families.”

Through St. Joseph, labor is transformed into cooperation with the Creator and an instrument of sanctification for oneself and others.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 24
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Glory of Domestic Life, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: Joseph loved Jesus as a father loves his son and showed his love by giving him the best he had.
scripture_or_quote.author: St. Josemaría Escrivá

reflection:
In the 16th century, St. Teresa of Avila buried medals of St. Joseph around her convents to place them under his protection. In the 20th century, St. André Bessette did the same on Mount Royal before building St. Joseph's Oratory.

**Saint Joseph wants to bless your home.** If you lovingly welcome St. Joseph into your home, invoke his intercession, and honor him in pious devotions, he will greatly bless your domestic life. Wherever St. Joseph is present, Jesus and Mary are present as well.

(A word of advice: Do not bury statues of St. Joseph upside down in yards to sell a house. Statues are meant to be venerated above ground with respect, not treated like magical talismans! Speak directly to St. Joseph with filial trust; he hears you.)

**Saint Joseph loves domestic life.** Saint Joseph is the saint of the hidden years of Jesus. Our Lord lived with Mary and St. Joseph for thirty years. Saint Joseph knew what Jesus’ walk sounded like, his laughter, his morning routine, and his favorite meals. These treasured memories reside deep in the heart and mind of St. Joseph.

> *Jesus and Mary themselves obey and offer their homage to Joseph, for they reverence what the hand of God has established in him.*  
> — Pope Pius XI

reading.title: Saint Joseph's Workshop
reading.content:
On March 19, 1963, St. Josemaría Escrivá delivered a beloved homily titled “In Joseph's Workshop.” He reflected:

“Joseph made Jesus a craftsman, transmitting his own professional skill to him. The neighbors of Nazareth called Jesus faber and fabri filius: the craftsman and the son of the craftsman. Jesus worked by Joseph's side. For Jesus must have resembled Joseph in his way of working, his speech, his eye for detail, the way he broke bread... Interior life is nothing but continual and direct conversation with Christ, so as to become one with him. And Joseph can tell us many things about Jesus. Therefore, never neglect devotion to him — Ite ad Ioseph: 'Go to Joseph'!”

In the workshop of Nazareth, ordinary carpentry became the holy ground where Jesus grew in wisdom and grace.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 25
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Guardian of Virgins, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: I prayed to St. Joseph to watch over me. From my childhood, my devotion to him was mingled with my love for the Blessed Virgin. Each day I recited the prayer, “O Saint Joseph, father and protector of virgins.” It seemed to me that I was well protected and completely sheltered from every danger.
scripture_or_quote.author: St. Thérèse of Lisieux

reflection:
Saint Joseph has a special love for those consecrated to God through religious vows. Saint Joseph loves everyone, of course, but he has a special place in his heart for virgins. A virgin himself, St. Joseph knows firsthand the intimacy that a virgin is capable of having with God. Saint Joseph lived for 30 years with the two greatest virgins to ever grace this planet: Jesus and Mary.

**Remember St. Joseph!** Saint Faustina’s religious community recited the *Memorare to St. Joseph* every day. Saint Faustina herself recorded how St. Joseph personally encouraged her in her mission of Divine Mercy.

**Saint Joseph will help you be a guardian of virginity and purity.** If you walk with St. Joseph, your eyes, thoughts, and relationships will be preserved from degrading influences. In times of temptation, run to St. Joseph!

> *I have taken for my advocate and protector, the glorious St. Joseph, to whom I have recommended myself with all the fervor of my heart, and by whom I have been visibly aided.*  
> — St. Teresa of Avila

reading.title: A Miraculous Staircase in New Mexico
reading.content:
In 1878, the Sisters of Loretto completed their chapel in Santa Fe, New Mexico, only to realize there was no staircase to the choir loft 20 feet above, and no floor space to build a conventional staircase. Having nowhere to turn, the sisters prayed a novena to St. Joseph.

On the ninth day, an unknown carpenter appeared leading a donkey with basic hand tools. Working in solitude for three months, he built an architectural marvel: a spiral staircase with two complete 360-degree turns, no central pole, no nails (held with wooden pegs), and constructed of spruce wood not native to the American Southwest.

When the staircase was finished, the craftsman disappeared without requesting payment or leaving a name. Wood technologists later confirmed the wood closely matched spruce native to Israel. The sisters have always believed that St. Joseph himself answered their novena.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 26
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Pillar of Families, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: Those who are devoted to prayer should, in a special manner, cherish devotion to St. Joseph. I know not how anyone can ponder on the sufferings, trials, and tribulations the Queen of Angels endured whilst caring for Jesus in his childhood, without at the same time thanking St. Joseph.
scripture_or_quote.author: St. Teresa of Avila

reflection:
Jesus, Mary, and Joseph love families. Their three hearts are very concerned about what is happening to families today. Modern man has attempted to redefine marriage and family, leading to broken homes, moral confusion, and spiritual desolation.

> *The final battle between the Lord and the kingdom of Satan will be about marriage and the family.*  
> — Servant of God Sr. Lucia of Fatima

**Saint Joseph wants to be the pillar of your family.** A pillar is a foundation. In order for your home to stand firm on rock, your family needs St. Joseph. He will teach your home prayer, mutual reverence, purity, forgiveness, and charity.

**Saint Joseph loves the family!** He teaches us the sanctifying reality of motherhood, fatherhood, and children. In St. Joseph, men discover what it means to be sacrificial protectors and loving fathers. A world filled with men who imitate St. Joseph will experience a great renewal of culture and family life.

> *I saw Jesus assisting his parents in every possible way... He assisted his foster-father in his trade, and devoted himself to prayer and contemplation.*  
> — Blessed Anne Catherine Emmerich

reading.title: Silent Witness
reading.content:
The Gospel does not record a single spoken word from St. Joseph: his language is silence (St. Pope Paul VI). Saint Joseph’s silence was not passivity; it was the sacred silence of adoration, humility, and prompt action.

Bishop Jacques-Bénigne Bossuet wrote: “The apostles are lights to make the world see Jesus. Joseph is a veil to cover him... He who makes the apostles glorious with the glory of preaching, glorifies Joseph by the humility of silence.”

In 1660, in Cotignac, France, St. Joseph appeared to shepherd Gaspard Ricard on a blazing hot day, instructing him to move a massive rock to find water. Eight men could barely budge the stone afterward, but from that spot a miraculous healing spring poured forth that continues to flow today. King Louis XIV consecrated France to St. Joseph as a result. Through his quiet strength, St. Joseph works wonders for all who trust in him.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 27
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Comfort of the Afflicted, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: Nothing will be refused him [St. Joseph], neither by Our Lady nor by his glorious Son.
scripture_or_quote.author: St. Francis de Sales

reflection:
Comforting the afflicted is a work of mercy. The Church gives us the Seven Spiritual and Seven Corporal Works of Mercy.

In Latin, *Solatium Miserorum* is translated as “Comfort of the Afflicted” or “Solace of Those in Misery.” Life in this valley of tears brings unexpected trials—financial hardships, illness, bereavement, and heartache.

**Saint Joseph will comfort you in difficult times.** He knows well the trials of life: homelessness at Bethlehem, refugee exile in Egypt, the pain of poverty, and the anxiety of losing Jesus for three days.

> *Let us commend ourselves to our good father, St. Joseph, who is the Patriarch of troubled people, since he himself went through so much trouble.*  
> — St. Joseph Marello

God wants you to rest in St. Joseph's fatherhood. Run to him when anxiety strikes. Pour out your worries to him. He is the most attentive and loving of fathers.

> *If discouragement overwhelms you, think of the faith of Joseph; if anxiety has its grip on you, think of the hope of Joseph.*  
> — Pope Benedict XVI

reading.title: Pious Union of St. Joseph
reading.content:
In 1913, St. Luigi Guanella, under the encouragement of Pope St. Pius X, founded the Pious Union of St. Joseph in Rome (San Giuseppe al Trionfale) as an international crusade of prayer for the suffering and dying. Pope St. Pius X became its very first enrolled member.

Saint Luigi Guanella spent his life caring for disabled children, abandoned elderly, and orphans, declaring: “Devotion to St. Joseph is necessary because the works of mercy are fruitless if they do not help souls acquire a holy and happy death like that of St. Joseph.”

Pope Leo XIII prayed: “My dear St. Joseph, be with me living, be with me dying, and obtain for me a favorable judgment from Jesus, my merciful Savior.”

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 28
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Hope of the Sick, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: As the Church’s Liturgy teaches, he [St. Joseph] “cooperated in the fullness of time in the great mystery of salvation” and is truly a “minister of salvation.”
scripture_or_quote.author: St. John Paul II

reflection:
God has healed countless people through the intercession of St. Joseph. Saint Teresa of Avila was cured of a crippling illness that left her near death after fervently invoking St. Joseph.

Saint Thérèse of Lisieux was saved from fatal infant illness through St. Joseph. When she was an infant and deathly ill, her mother St. Zélie Martin knelt before a statue of St. Joseph in tears, commending the child to his care. Within fifteen minutes, little Thérèse opened her eyes and began nursing vigorously!

**Saint Joseph offers hope in times of sickness.** If you or someone you love suffers from illness, turn to St. Joseph. He will obtain physical healing according to God's holy will, or the spiritual strength to unite your suffering with Christ's Passion.

> *Like St. Joseph, let us live each day according to the dispositions of providence, doing whatever God suggests.*  
> — St. Joseph Marello

reading.title: Votive Masses
reading.content:
A long-standing Church tradition designates each day of the week with a particular theme: Wednesday is the day consecrated to honoring St. Joseph (falling halfway between the Lord's Day on Sunday and Our Lady's Saturday). Blessed Anna Maria Taigi fasted on bread and water every Wednesday in honor of St. Joseph.

March is St. Joseph's month, celebrated worldwide with the Solemnity of St. Joseph on March 19 and traditions like the Sicilian St. Joseph's Altar, feeding the poor and honoring his paternal provision.

Blessed Mary of Providence founded the Helpers of the Holy Souls under St. Joseph's patronage. Saint Joseph assured Sr. Mary Martha Chambon: “If the soul who prayed to me still has debts to pay to the Sovereign Judge, I shall ask for grace on its behalf.”

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 29
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Patron of the Dying, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: The name of Joseph will be our protection during all the days of our life, but above all at the moment of death.
scripture_or_quote.author: Blessed William Joseph Chaminade

reflection:
Saint Joseph died the most holy and enviable death in human history: he passed into eternity gazing upon Jesus and resting in the arms of Mary. For this reason, God designated him the Patron of a Happy Death.

At the hour of death, a great spiritual battle takes place for the soul. We need our spiritual father's presence to fortify us and banish despair.

> *Jesus granted to him [St. Joseph] the special privilege of safeguarding the dying against the snares of Lucifer, just as he had also saved him from the schemes of Herod.*  
> — St. Alphonsus Liguori

**Saint Joseph is your personal patron.** None of us will remain here forever. To prevent an unprepared death without the Sacraments, consecrate yourself now to St. Joseph. Walk in sanctifying grace, go to Confession, and stay close to your father's side.

> *Happy are you if your death has the assistance of St. Joseph. The prayers of St. Joseph will throw around you an all-protecting mantle of defense.*  
> — Venerable Nelson Baker

reading.title: Patron of a Happy Death
reading.content:
Tradition holds that St. Joseph died before Jesus began his public ministry and Passion. Saint Bernardine of Siena notes that had Joseph been present at Calvary, Christ's entrustment of Mary to St. John would have caused confusion for the early Church; God took Joseph to himself beforehand in holy peace.

Many saints—including St. Bernardine of Siena, St. Francis de Sales, Pope St. John XXIII, and St. George Preca—piously believed that St. Joseph was among the saints who rose from the dead at Christ's Resurrection (Mt 27:52) and was assumed bodily into heaven to participate in the Lord's ascension!

Venerable Mary of Ágreda wrote that St. Joseph's true cause of death was love: his heart could hold no more adoration and loving sacrifice, and he was consumed in the love of Jesus and Mary.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 30
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Terror of Demons, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: Jesus, Mary, and Joseph pursued their way through many towns of Egypt, driving out the demons not only from the idols, but out of many bodies possessed by them.
scripture_or_quote.author: Venerable Mary of Ágreda

reflection:
Demons fear Jesus. Demons fear Mary. And demons are absolutely terrified of St. Joseph!

Evil spirits fear St. Joseph because he alone is the spouse of the Immaculata and the earthly father of Jesus Christ. Everything that touched him became holy. He saved the Savior from Herod, spent decades in adoration, and exercised paternal authority over the Son of God.

**Saint Joseph is a dragon slayer!** The title “Terror of Demons” (*Terror Daemonum*) is the most unique title of St. Joseph. It is the title of a warrior. The white lily he holds is a spiritual lance of purity that pierces every demonic snare. Demons fear him even when he sleeps, because they know his spirit is constantly vigilant for God.

**Saint Joseph will protect you against Satan and his demons.** In times of spiritual oppression, temptation, and fear, call upon the holy name of St. Joseph!

> *Saint Joseph, may you and your immaculate spouse assist me in the final struggle.*  
> — St. John Neumann

reading.title: Terror of Demons
reading.content:
Blessed Bartolo Longo, who was rescued from being an ordained satanic priest through the Rosary and devotion to St. Joseph, wrote: “The name of St. Joseph makes demons tremble and flee!”

Lucifer hates fatherhood because all true fatherhood reflects God the Father. When men embrace the sacrificial, pure fatherhood of St. Joseph, Satan's power over families is broken. Impurity leaves men spiritually powerless; the purity of St. Joseph is a lethal weapon against every dark perversion.

Pope Leo XIII forged together the two greatest spiritual weapons—the Rosary and St. Joseph—prescribing the prayer *To You, O Blessed Joseph* to be prayed at the end of every October Rosary.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 31
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: Protector of the Holy Church, Pray for Us

scripture_or_quote.quote: The Church invokes St. Joseph as her Patron and Protector through her unshakable trust that he to whom Christ willed to confide the care and protection of his own frail childhood, will continue from heaven to perform his protective task in order to guide and defend the Mystical Body of Christ.
scripture_or_quote.author: St. Pope Paul VI

reflection:
The Church needs the protection of St. Joseph today more than ever. The Church is assaulted by external enemies and wounded by internal scandals and lukewarmness.

Jesus never promised that every individual in the Church would be holy—the wheat and weeds grow together until the harvest. Our role is to remain close to St. Joseph so that we remain wheat, not weeds.

**Saint Joseph protects the Church.** No matter what scandals or trials occur, do not lose heart! God will never abandon his Church, and St. Joseph will never abandon the bride of his Son.

Blessed Miguel Pro, who was martyred in Mexico with a crucifix in one hand, rosary in the other, and St. Joseph in his heart, said: “The splendor of the Resurrection is already on its way because now the gloom of the Passion is at its height.”

> *Hold fast to Jesus, Mary, and St. Joseph. They are with us. Trust in Divine Providence.*

reading.title: Patron of the Universal Church
reading.content:
In 1868, Blessed Jean-Joseph Lataste, a French Dominican priest devoted to prisoners, made a vow to God offering his own life as a sacrifice if the Pope would declare St. Joseph Patron of the Universal Church. Pope Pius IX was deeply moved by his letter: “Father Lataste will shortly be granted his wish... he is the only one who offered his life.”

Blessed Jean-Joseph died in 1869 at age 36. Exactly one year later, on December 8, 1870, Blessed Pope Pius IX promulgated the solemn decree *Quemadmodum Deus*, declaring St. Joseph Patron of the Universal Church!

Just as Joseph in Egypt provided for the entire kingdom, St. Joseph protects and nourishes the whole Catholic Church until the end of time.

prayer.title: Daily Prayer for Day 32
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph.

title: He Made Him the Lord of His Household, and Prince Over All His Possessions

scripture_or_quote.quote: As Almighty God appointed Joseph, son of the patriarch Jacob, over all the land of Egypt to save grain for the people, so when the fullness of time was come... he chose another Joseph and made him the lord and chief of his household.
scripture_or_quote.author: Blessed Pope Pius IX

reflection:
Our spiritual father St. Joseph is lord, chief, and guardian of the treasures of heaven!

When the mother of James and John asked Jesus for her sons to sit at his right and left hand in the Kingdom (Mt 20:20-28), Jesus replied that those places were reserved for those for whom it has been prepared by his Father. Mary sits at Jesus' right hand as Queen Mother. Who sits at his left? It is fitting that St. Joseph occupies that exalted throne, because no saint is greater than the father of Jesus Christ!

> *It is a monstrous crime for a father to be poor while the son lives in abundance. Who could imagine that the son of God, who is master of all virtues, would forget Joseph whom he loved and cherished as his father?*  
> — Blessed William Joseph Chaminade

**Saint Joseph is your increaser.** Let him increase your intimacy with Jesus and Mary. He is your all-powerful intercessor. Today, you stand on the threshold of total consecration!

> *Joseph is an all-powerful intercessor. In that way we shall greatly please Jesus and Mary, who consider as done for themselves what is done for Joseph.*  
> — St. Peter Julian Eymard

reading.title: Consecration Day
reading.content:
You’ve made it! Today you consecrate yourself entirely to St. Joseph.

A comprehensive program of consecration to St. Joseph has taken centuries to develop. It is now revealed, and you have been chosen by God to receive a tremendous blessing in the spiritual life. You are part of the dawn of the Era of St. Joseph!

For the rest of your life, love, trust, and honor St. Joseph. Go to him in times of plenty, in times of poverty, in good times and in bad. He will be your guardian, your strength, and your certainty of not being lost. If you become weary, go to Joseph. If you become anxious, go to Joseph. When tempted, run to St. Joseph!

Never forget what you have learned in these 33 days. Renew your consecration frequently. You are now consecrated to St. Joseph—go forth and be an apparition of St. Joseph for the world!

prayer.title: Consecration Prayer
prayer.instruction: Pray the Litany of St. Joseph, followed by the Act of Consecration to St. Joseph.
